title: M. R. Jayakar
summary: Argued for deferring further consideration of the Objectives Resolution so absent parties could participate and the Assembly's work would not be frustrated.

title: B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya
summary: Pressed the procedural character and priority of Jayakar's postponement proposal during the amendment debate.

title: Mohan Lal Saksena
summary: On 16 December raised the rule that an amendment should be formally moved before the speech; on 18 December proposed changes to the Rules Committee schedule.

title: K. Santhanam
summary: On 16 December challenged the internal logic of Jayakar's legal argument; on 18 December proposed taking completed portions of the Rules before the House.

title: N. V. Gadgil
summary: Rejected the claim that the relevant Cabinet Mission clause prohibited the Assembly from proceeding at the preliminary stage.

title: R. K. Sidhwa
summary: On 16 December disputed using the absence of the States as a reason for delay; on 18 December defended minority security and opposed separate electorates.

title: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
summary: On 16 December rejected additions to the accepted Cabinet Mission basis; on 18 December insisted that Constituent Assembly business and the Rules take priority.

title: Suresh Chandra Banerjee
summary: Pressed the practical question of how long the Assembly should wait if the Muslim League continued to stay away.

title: Govind Ballabh Pant
summary: Challenged Jayakar's interpretation of the princely States' likely conduct and objected to speaking for them without their representatives.

title: Hari Singh Gour
summary: Attempted to introduce a wider proposal on communal representation; the Chair ruled the proposed amendment out of order.

title: Diwan Chaman Lall
summary: Argued that Jayakar's proposal was substantive rather than merely procedural because it also altered the constitutional proposition.

title: Somnath Lahiri
summary: Defended an expansive amendment as action flowing from the Resolution's aims; the Chair ruled it out but promised him speaking time on the main Resolution.

title: Syamanandan Sahaya
summary: Proposed wording changes around the Republic, Union, the States and popular sovereignty to reduce barriers to wider participation.

title: N. G. Ranga
summary: Questioned whether multiple amendments should permit repeated speeches by the same member.

title: Uday Chand Mahtab
summary: Declined to move his listed amendment when called by the Chair.

title: Shri Krishna Sinha
summary: Supported the original Resolution and emphasised popular sovereignty, a democratic decentralised republic and safeguards for minorities.

title: Purushottam Das Tandon
summary: Seconded the Objectives Resolution on 13 December; on 18 December argued that members and parties needed adequate time to study the Assembly Rules.

title: M. R. Masani
summary: Read the Objectives Resolution through democratic socialism, individual liberty and the long-term transformation of minorities into a common nation.

title: Frank Anthony
summary: Supported Dr. Jayakar’s amendment to defer parts of the declaration in the interest of wider agreement and participation.

title: Syama Prasad Mookerjee
summary: Opposed postponement and argued that the Assembly’s ultimate political sanction came from the people of India.

title: Sardar Ujjal Singh
summary: Supported the Resolution while placing Sikh minority safeguards, Punjab and opposition to partition squarely before the House.

title: Seth Govind Das
summary: Spoke in Hindustani, connected freedom with democratic-socialist aspiration and urged the Assembly to continue despite external obstruction.

title: Ananthasayanam Ayyangar
summary: Requested a full Christmas-week recess before the Assembly resumed in the new year.

title: Hriday Nath Kunzru
summary: Raised scheduling concerns and then defended postponement of the Objectives Resolution as a way to strengthen participation and the Assembly’s moral authority.

title: Dhirendra Nath Datta
summary: Asked for more time to scrutinise the Rules and later made a brief interjection during the debate on grouping.

title: J. J. M. Nichols-Roy
summary: Supported the Resolution, defended religious freedom and minority security, and argued that autonomous units could coexist with a democratic Indian Union.

title: Debi Prasad Khaitan
summary: Argued that Constituent Assembly work and completion of the Rules should take precedence over other engagements.

title: Sri Biswanath Das
summary: Supported the Resolution, discussed grouping and popular sovereignty in the States, and rebutted claims that the Assembly was a caste-Hindu body.

title: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar
summary: Opposed postponement, asserted broad constituent power and argued that real constitutional authority in Indian States must derive from their people.
